To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
live-attenuate influenza vaccine elicits higher magnitude T-cell response to the rapidly evolving HAs of influenza A viruses.

TIV elicits higher antibody responses, whereas LAIV elicits superior T-cell responses, and LAIV elicits higher magnitude T-cell response toward the variant region of HA, which is prone to antibody escape.
the live attenuated influenza vaccine (Flumist®) elicits stronger T-cell responses than the inactivated influenza vaccine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
influenza vaccines, which are currently the only licensed and approved influenza vaccines.
understanding the immunological basis of influenza vaccine-induced protection and the mechanisms underlying the induction of protective immunity.
understanding how influenza viruses interact with their hosts and how the host responds to infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LAIV elicits superior T cell responses compared with TIV.
both TIV and LAIV are equally effective in protecting against influenza infection.
both vaccines elicit robust and durable immune responses, and both are safe and effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the live-attenedated influenza vaccine elicits superior T-cell response than the inactivated influenza vaccine.
TIV and LAIV induce distinct immune responses against influenza, and the magnitude of T-cell response is significantly higher with LAIV.
the T-cell responses eliciting by live-attenuate influenza vaccines are superior to those elicited by inactivated influenza vaccine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T-cell responses eliciting by the LAIV were superior to those elicited by the TIV, and that the LAIV elicited T cells that recognized the rapidly evolving variant region of the H3N2 HA.
LAIV elicits superior T-cell responses against the rapidly mutating HA antigenic sites.
T-cell responses eliciting by LAIV are more robust and cross-protective than antibody responses elicited by TIV.
